C4-F5 (60-77) on 18 tubes, F#5-G5 (78-79) on 20-tube sets (Adler, App. A; Piston 60-77). Max 2 notes at once per player. No fast melodic runs; a fast pedalled figure = pealing bells (Adler). Real bells below C4 are impossible: imitate orchestrally (Piston). Perceived pitch can seem an octave off because of the strike tone (general knowledge).

registers.name: common set
registers.character: written C5-C6; pure, piercing, long ring

notes: Sounds two octaves higher (Adler). Older scores vary (sounding as written or an octave higher), so period parts may lie lower, e.g. Berlioz Bb5/F6 (82, 89). Hand-held pairs: one pair = one pitch (Piston).

registers.name: whole range
registers.character: struck metal strings; florid fast figuration cuts through tutti

notes: Four chromatic octaves E2-E6 (Adler p.449-450). Sustained notes are rolls even if not marked. Damper pedal on most instruments. Hungarian colour (Piston p.338-339). Also covered in mallet-percussion-extended-and-rare.
Unpitched: MIDI note = library key map (GM 38). Ostinati, rolls.
No snares; deeper than the snare; processional. Library key map.
Unpitched (GM 35/36). Most powerful instrument; speaks slightly late; damping makes durations meaningful.
Unpitched (GM crash 49/57). Let ring or damp; pp possible.
Unpitched; library key map. Two-mallet roll crescendo booster; do not overuse.
Unpitched; dark, shuddering, long decay; violent when struck hard. Use very sparingly; soft strokes most effective (Piston); never repeat quickly.
Unpitched (GM 80 muted / 81 open). Audible over the tutti; use sparingly. Extreme economy; soft dynamics best (Adler).
Unpitched (GM 54). Hits, shakes, rolls. Sizes 38/25/15 cm; 25 cm if unspecified (Adler). Struck, shaken roll (loud), thumb roll (soft).
Unpitched (GM 76 high / 77 low). High, hard, dry; usually three sizes.
Unpitched; library key map. Orchestral machine castanets on a handle.

registers.name: lowest
registers.character: deep, long ring; muddy in close chords; a single wound string lacks body (Piston)

registers.name: low-middle
registers.character: full, warm; bass notes, open arpeggios; best melodic zone begins (Piston)

registers.name: high
registers.character: bright, clear, shorter ring; no expressive melody (Piston)

weak_dynamics.issue: short and weak (general knowledge)
strings too short for expressive melody (Piston p.338)
single low note lacks carrying power: enharmonic unison or doubling (Piston p.327)
covered by brass/tutti except glissandi and middle-register ff chords

notes: 47 strings in Cb major. Range variants: Adler (chapter, App. A) 23-104 (G pedal reaches the top string), Piston 23-102 (1955). Lowest string(s) have no pedal: fixed per piece (Adler: two lowest, 23-26; Piston: lowest). 7 pedals (D C B | E F G A), one setting per letter in all octaves; pitch classes 2, 7, 9 (D, G, A) have no homophone. Max 4 notes and 16 st per hand, chords rolled upward by default. Harmonics sound +12, strings 45-77 (sounding 57-89, Adler); RH 1, LH 2-3. See harp-pedals, harp-techniques.

weak_dynamics.issue: quiet unamplified; harmonics nearly inaudible; thin the orchestra (Adler p.102)

notes: Written treble clef an octave above sounding. Open strings 40 45 50 55 59 64; chan 0-5 = strings 1-6. Adler chapter chart and App. A top 76; 19-fret instrument to 83 (general knowledge); Ample Guitar L plays 40-84. Solo writing: classical-guitar-solo.

registers.name: whole range
registers.character: bright plucked; held notes only as tremolo

weak_dynamics.issue: quiet: solo or with pizz/muted strings, soft winds (Adler p.104)

notes: 4 paired courses tuned like the violin, 55 62 69 76. Plectrum. Sustain = tremolo. Practical = Adler App. A pro range G3-E6.

weak_dynamics.issue: covered by horns/saxes at p (Gershwin, Adler p.107)

notes: Adler tuning C3 G3 B3/C4 D4 + thumb string G4 (48 55 59/60 62 67); bluegrass open G 50 55 59 62 67 (general knowledge). Each fretted string reaches a M9 above open. Practical top = Adler's chart A4 [?] (App. A shows only C3 and A4 and calls the banjo non-transposing; tenor banjo 8vb, 36-57). Transposition -12 is general knowledge.

registers.name: bass
registers.character: percussive; reinforces timpani/BD (Adler); loud staccato turns metallic and hides pitch (Piston)

registers.name: middle
registers.character: full, singing; least useful for orchestral doubling (Adler prefers extremes)

registers.name: treble
registers.character: bright, short decay; adds brilliance to piccolo/flute up to 108 (Piston)

notes: Orchestral use: doubler (pizz, staccato winds, xylophone, accents) in short values, not on legato pads; percussion (low tremolo with timp/BD rolls). CC64 damper; sostenuto (CC66) only below middle C and missing on many pianos. Per hand <= 5 notes, <= ~16 st span.

weak_dynamics.issue: soft instrument: disappears in loud textures

notes: Written C3-C7, sounds an octave higher (Adler App. A agrees; its extra top note is unreadable, do not use). Sweet spot ~72-96 (inferred from Adler). Medium decay: no true staccato (resonators ring, Adler) and no long sustain (Piston). Doubles harp, flutes/piccolo, pizz or muted solo violins on the same chord tones.

weak_dynamics.issue: very limited volume: thin the orchestration around it

notes: Dynamics only via stops/coupler and texture; thin the orchestra around it or play in its rests (Adler); avoid against a large orchestra unless amplified/modern high-power (Adler, Piston). Baroque continuo. Adler App. A: F1-F6 (29-89); chapter top read uncertainly (F6 or E6), Piston bottom F1 [?].

registers.name: manual key range
registers.character: colour and loudness set by registration

notes: Ranges are KEY numbers at 8' pitch; 16' stops sound -12, 4' +12. No touch dynamics. Adler App. A: common 56-key manuals C2-G6 (36-91); 61-key manuals reach C7 (96).

KEY numbers; with a 16' stop the sounding pitch is -12, 32' -24 (inferred). Score marks +16'/+32' to extend down; most organs lack 32' (Adler). Sustained notes only; low pedal cluster (C-C#-D) for storm effects (Piston, Verdi Otello). Adler App. A: common 25-note pedalboard C2-C4 (36-60); 32-note pedalboards reach G4 (67).

registers.name: five-octave compass
registers.character: soft sustained reed tone; stops colour and extend +/-12

notes: Adler ex.13-12 and App. A: F1-F6, low F1 and top read uncertainly [?]; some instruments reach C7 (96); some stops extend an octave up/down. Write like organ manuals, no pedalboard. Soft chords under recitative; small-orchestra wind substitute (Piston).
